from.place: Opening compactification step: prove that vertical hyperdescent plus transition equivalences is exactly hyperdescent for the generated total-site topology; the local lower-refinement condition controls pullbacks of mixed covers.

title: Hyperdescent for the generated total-site topology
statement: Let $I$ be a small poset and let $i\mapsto\mathcal C_i$ be a strict covariant diagram of small Grothendieck sites [def-weil-size-convention], with transition functors $\iota_{ij}:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal C_j$ that are full-sieve inclusions (full, and with every arrow whose target is in the image having source in the image). Form $\mathcal E$ with objects $(i,T)$, $T\in\mathcal C_i$, and arrows $(i,T)\to(j,S)$ for $i\le j$ given by arrows $\iota_{ij}T\to S$ in $\mathcal C_j$. Assume the local lower-refinement condition: for $i,j\le k$, $T\in\mathcal C_i$, $S\in\mathcal C_j$, and an arrow $S\to T$ in $\mathcal C_k$, there is a covering family $\{S_\alpha\to S\}$ in $\mathcal C_j$ and indices $l_\alpha\le i,j$ such that each $S_\alpha$ is in the image of $\mathcal C_{l_\alpha}\to\mathcal C_j$. Give $\mathcal E$ the topology generated by vertical covering families and singleton identity-underlying transition arrows $(i,T)\to(j,\iota_{ij}T)$. Let $\mathbf D(\Lambda)$ be the enhanced derived category of complexes of modules over a commutative ring $\Lambda$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. A coherent presheaf means an enhanced functor $F:\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf D(\Lambda)$ with the higher naturality data of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Then, for every fixed integer $a$, such an $F$ is a hypersheaf (its value on every hypercover $T_\bullet\to T$ maps equivalently to $\operatorname{holim}_{[n]\in\Delta}F(T_n)$) and has $H^r(F(i,T))=0$ for $r<a$ if and only if each fibre presheaf $F_i$ is a hypersheaf on $\mathcal C_i$ with the same pointwise lower bound and all transition restriction maps are equivalences. This equivalence is natural under restriction to subposets.
